features.description: Public MCP transport: a dedicated frontend route to the FastMCP /mcp server that survives the trailing-slash redirect, plus a deployed Streamable-HTTP smoke script.
acceptance_criteria: Extract shared forwardToBackend(req, backendPath) from the catch-all proxy without changing /api/proxy/** behaviour
frontend/src/app/api/mcp/route.ts forwards GET/POST/DELETE/OPTIONS to backend 'mcp/' (trailing slash) with SSE passthrough + duplex:half + Mcp-Session-Id passthrough
scripts/smoke-deployed-mcp.sh: a streamablehttp_client probe that initialize + list_tools anonymously against <frontend-url>/api/mcp, mirroring scripts/smoke-deployed.sh URL resolution
Local: frontend route proxies POST to backend /mcp/ returning 200 (not 502/308)
Existing /api/proxy/** routes and skill tools unchanged
features.notes: Done. Extracted forwardToBackend() to frontend/src/lib/backendProxy.ts; catch-all refactored to use it (8 existing tests still green); /api/mcp/route.ts forwards to backend 'mcp/' (trailing slash); scripts/smoke-deployed-mcp.sh added (streamablehttp_client probe, REQUIRE_SIMS gate). 4 new route tests + 8 catch-all tests pass; quality:check:fast clean. Local-verify covered by unit tests + existing test_mcp_server.py (POSTs /mcp/ -> 200); end-to-end deployed verify is M3.

features.description: Register every bridge-speaking artefact as a ui:// MCP App resource + show_<name> tool on the deployed FastMCP server, additively (skill tools unchanged). Resolve backend artefact availability.
acceptance_criteria: register_sim_apps(mcp) in backend/protocols/mcp_server.py ports the PoC discover_artefacts(): for each artefact, a FunctionResource (uri ui://aipla/<name>/<ver>, mime_type text/html;profile=mcp-app) + mcp.add_tool(show_fn, name show_<name>, meta {ui.resourceUri + visibility, openai/outputTemplate})
register_sim_apps(mcp) called once from get_mcp_asgi_app() after rebuild_tools()

Artefact availability resolved: backend can read the artefact HTML at runtime (bake into backend image via Dockerfile COPY if build context allows, else read from the sandbox URL) — chosen approach documented in code + sprint notes

tests/api_tests/test_mcp_server.py extended: tools/list includes show_boldkast|kinebot|led_planck with _meta.ui.resourceUri; resources/read of a ui:// URI returns text/html;profile=mcp-app HTML containing 'ui/initialize'; existing skill-tool tests still pass
cd backend && make lint && make test-fast green
features.notes: Done. backend/protocols/sim_apps.py: discover_sims() (FS scan when present, else KNOWN_SIMS) + register_sim_apps(mcp) registers each as a FunctionResource (ui://aipla/<name>/<ver>, mime text/html;profile=mcp-app, lazy load_html) + show_<name> tool with meta {ui.resourceUri+visibility, openai/outputTemplate}. Wired into get_mcp_asgi_app() (defensive try/except). Artefact availability: FS-first (dev/CI/tests read the repo path), lazy sandbox-URL fetch in prod via MCP_SANDBOX_URL (derived from the existing _MCP_SANDBOX_URL substitution) — NO Dockerfile bake, NO git duplication, NO startup network. DEVIATION from plan: no backend/Dockerfile change; instead M3 adds MCP_SANDBOX_URL to the sidecar env in cloudbuild. Gotcha fixed: tool fn must have zero params (FastMCP turns params into inputSchema; _title default-arg rejected) -> factory closure. Test-isolation fix: extended _clean_registry autouse fixture to also clear sim tools (they register on the shared instance at app import, leaking into the rebuild_tools tool-list assertions). 4 new tests; make lint + make test-fast green (2274 passed).

features.notes: Done. cloudbuild: +MCP_SANDBOX_URL on the sidecar. Pushed (rebased onto an incoming deps patch). Deploy ran ~25min (ADK backend image slow) — aipla-dev-deploy check-run green. Verified deployed: REQUIRE_SIMS smoke + a direct resources/read both PASS on https://aipla-v01-frontend-wgwhd7mspa-lz.a.run.app/api/mcp (anonymous Streamable HTTP; 4 skill tools + show_boldkast/kinebot/led_planck; ui://aipla/boldkast/v1 read returns 34269 bytes text/html;profile=mcp-app with the bridge — lazy sandbox fetch works in prod). Docs updated (design Implemented + host caveat, WORKSHOP/README cloud path, deployed-urls, SEQUENCE) + memory. Live VISUAL render is host-dependent: Claude Desktop recognises the UI resource but doesn't mount the iframe (upstream claude-ai-mcp#165; the MCP Python SDK 1.27 has no MCP Apps support, our hand-rolled metadata is spec-correct); ChatGPT/Inspector are the reliable checks. Acceptance #1/#2/#4 met; #3 (visual render) host-blocked on Claude Desktop, reliable elsewhere; #5 exposure dev-only/authorised.
